target:
The leak check misses Windows paths because of how it builds the text it searches.

**Cause (verified):** `leaks()` in `src/leaks.py:8` runs `json.dumps(actions)` before searching. JSON escapes every backslash, so a transcript containing `C:\Users\dana` is searched as `c:\\users\\dana`. The secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so the substring match fails. The forward-slash path has no backslashes, so `/home/dana` survives the encoding and gets caught. I confirmed this with a read-only one-liner: the transcript text was `c:\\users\\dana`, the single-backslash secret returned `False`, and the double-backslash form returned `True`.

**Regression test (verified):** I added `test_a_windows_home_folder_in_a_command_is_found` to `tests/test_leaks.py`, following the project's CLAUDE.md. It fails on every run I made (two runs, both with the same assertion: `[] != ['C:\\Users\\dana']`). I left it in place as the regression test. It is uncommitted.

**Scope:**
- I did not touch `src/`. `git status` shows only `README.md` (already modified before I started), `tests/test_leaks.py` (my test), and the untracked `notes/`.
- I added no print or debug lines to any file.

**Inferred, not checked:** Any secret containing a backslash, quote, or control character is affected the same way, since those are also escaped by `json.dumps`. A possible fix for the other session's owner is to search each record's raw string fields instead of the dumped JSON, or to escape the secrets the same way before matching. I did not verify either approach.
